newsitem.title: INDIA: HUNDREDS OF HINDU PILGRIMS STRANDED IN SNOWFALL.
newsitem.headline: HUNDREDS OF HINDU PILGRIMS STRANDED IN SNOWFALL.

text.p: Hundreds of Hindus on a Himalayan pilgrimage were stranded on Friday due to heavy snowfall in northern India, local government officials said.
They said the pilgrimage to the sacred mountain cave of Amarnath in the state of Jammu and Kashmir had been indefinitely suspended until the snow stopped. No casualties were reported.

At least 214 pilgrims died last year after bitter winds and heavy snow lashed the trail to Amarnath, located 12,500 feet (3,846 metres) above sea level, some 330 km (200 miles) northeast of the state's winter capital Jammu.
Since the pilgrimage began on July 16, more than 24,000 pilgrims have visited the cave, where they worship an ice stalagmite believed to be a symbol of Lord Shiva, the Hindu god of regeneration.
The 5,000-year-old cave's chief priest says he expects 120,000 pilgrims to visit Amarnath this year.
